So the Phillips curve posits that there is a relationship between the  degree of slack in the labor market and inflation, and it is an empirical relationship that, while  not absolutely tight, has been a consistent relationship over time, and I believe that relationship  still holds.

In addition, the Phillips curve theory suggests that inflation expectations are also an  important driver of actual wage- and price-setting decisions and inflation behavior, and I believe  there’s also solid empirical evidence for that.
But this model continues to at least influence  my own thinking, and it certainly is a factor that I and at least some of my colleagues are  incorporating in these projections.
